parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent integrated changes in the single workspace, committed requirement patches, rebuilt tracked binaries, cleaned transient result blocks, and delivered a final implementation summary.

serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all analysis, editing, debugging, commits, verification, cleanup, and final delivery in a single parent trajectory with no child delegation.
serial.implementation: Implemented buffer primitives, tuple helpers, selection, projection, external sort, all joins, tree printing, parser, optimizer, then added a final runtime stabilization commit.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built both applications, recorded requirement patches and commits, removed generated result blocks, and left rebuilt executables in the working tree for delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the 26 hollow database-lab requirements across QueryProcessing and QueryOptimize and asked children to inspect the two code areas.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial read the same requirement set and source map without child delegation before implementing the same family of modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage advantage appears; both claimed full requirement coverage and both official evaluations failed the same named result entries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by spawning QueryProcessing and QueryOptimize analysis children, while the parent retained implementation and commit ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all analysis, implementation, debugging, and commits inside one parent trajectory with an explicit sequential plan.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete difference is advisory parallel analysis versus single-actor analysis; ownership of durable source changes stayed with the parent in both attempts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child handoffs identified TODO inventories and optimizer implementation advice, but they did not create separately owned interfaces or component contracts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial derived interfaces directly from headers, source stubs, data layout, and drivers in one context without handoff boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No harmful context transfer is evidenced: the parallel handoffs were advisory and not the source of the final parser, join, or output failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented buffer I/O, tuple helpers, external sort, selection, projection, joins, parser, tree output, and optimizer, including a hash join correction before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the same broad modules and added a post-verification runtime stabilization commit for quiet cleanup and hash-join probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementation paths converged strongly; serial shows an explicit late stabilization commit, while parallel also debugged hash join and claimed all joins reached 303 tuples before finalization.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The two children completed and returned advisory findings; no child implementation or verifier result remained trapped or unjoined.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all observations and fixes stayed in the single parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra child-result handling, but the returned work was advice rather than deliverable code, so no result lifecycle failure was retained.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent made the durable edits, generated requirement patches, built binaries, and cleaned transient generated data blocks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial likewise made source commits, cleaned generated blocks, and left rebuilt executable artifacts modified after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concurrent shared-state collision is visible because the parallel children did not write source files or deliverables.

comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on similar local smoke checks that missed the official evaluator assertions around tuple content, I/O labels, join outputs, and optimizer pushdown.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both current completed status.json evaluations report solution_passed false. The concrete task-solving difference is procedural rather than outcome-determining: parallel used two advisory child agents for code-area analysis while the parent performed the implementation, integration, commits, local builds, smoke tests, cleanup, and final answer; serial performed comparable implementation and verification in one trajectory and added an explicit final runtime stabilization commit. Both attempts converged on local evidence that all joins returned 303 tuples and both missed the same evaluator-sensitive failures around tuple contents, I/O output expectations, join assertions, and two optimizer pushdown checks.
parallel_contributors: Two child agents supplied advisory inspection of QueryProcessing and QueryOptimize, but durable implementation and verification remained parent-owned.
serial_contributors: The serial parent performed the same broad implementation path without child handoffs and committed a final runtime stabilization fix.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The residual failures are best treated as ordinary implementation or acceptance-coverage defects shared by both runs, not as a parallel coordination consequence.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator exposed stricter output-content and optimizer expectations than either run covered with local smoke checks.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; no retained parallel-side coordination pattern

Rejected: the parent produced the final response and left built binaries; no child deliverable or entry point was stranded without assembly ownership.
Rejected: the parent maintained an end-to-end plan from requirements through implementation, builds, smoke checks, cleanup, and closure.
Rejected: no mandatory serial preflight blocked productive implementation; the children ran as advisory scans while the parent continued planning and coding.
Rejected: the two children investigated narrow areas, but their advisory phase did not gate all later implementation or leave a shortened closure window.
Rejected: the indispensable implementation path was not starved; the parent carried the main critical path and completed broad source changes.
Rejected: the parallel run used only two completed children, stayed far inside the official timeout, and shows no fan-out budget exhaustion.
Rejected: the QueryProcessing child had broad inspection scope but no required child-owned implementation was left unfinished or needed for delivery.
Rejected: even if child briefs were concise, the children returned usable analysis and no missing delegated requirement made their work unusable or caused unmet child-owned delivery.
Rejected: no separately owned child implementations were expected to interoperate, so no cross-agent interface contract failure materialized.
Rejected: no known requirement, finding, checkpoint, or file-state fact is shown disappearing between actors and causing repeated or wrong work.
Rejected: the returned child reports were concise enough to inspect, and no dependent implementation step was abandoned because the handoff was too large.
Rejected: the parent did not consume a child report that described a superseded workspace state and then act inconsistently with newer observable state.
Rejected: the child reports did not present incompatible contracts that remained unadjudicated at an integration decision point.
Rejected: the parent ran builds and local whole-command smoke checks before finalizing; the later hidden official failures alone do not establish a parent-visible unsupported completion boundary.
Rejected: the parallel trajectory has no replacement or retry child that was restarted without inherited findings and repeated prior work.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; no candidate had both a qualifying parallel coordination boundary and a realized adverse consequence.
